nodes.name: Solvothermal Ni/Co(OH)₂ growth on Ru@NF
nodes.procedure: Cobalt nitrate hexahydrate (Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 1.51 mmol) and cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB, 1.37 mmol) were dissolved in a solution involving methanol (30 mL) and ultrapure water (6 mL), and ultrasonicated for 5 min. Afterward, the solution and Ru@NF were added to a Teflon-lined autoclave (50 mL) and then placed in an oven set to 160°C for a period of 20 h. Following a cooling period to 25°C, the Ni/Co(OH)₂-Ru@NF material was prepared.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/Co(OH)₂-Ru@NF shows the morphology of microspheres attached to sheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) characterizations indicate that Ru species grew as separated blocks on the NF surface ... Notably, with the fabrication of Ni/Co(OH)₂, Ni/Co(OH)₂-Ru@NF shows the morphology of microspheres attached to sheets (Figure 1c1-c3; Figure S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Co, Ru, Ni, O, and C elements on Ni/Co(OH)₂-Ru@NF surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1d and Figure S4 (Supporting Information) illustrate the uniform distribution of Co, Ru, Ni, O, and C on the Ni/Co(OH)₂-Ru@NF surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Catalyst formed by large number of microparticles and sheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images show that the catalyst is formed by a large number of microparticles and sheets, as displayed in Figure 2a,b.

nodes.characterization_summary: Heterointerfaces observed with lattice fringes of 0.232 nm (Co(OH)₂ (002)), 0.175 nm (Ni(OH)₂ (012)), and 0.205 nm (Ru (101)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2c, the heterointerfaces for Co(OH)₂ Ni(OH)₂-Ru can be clearly determined. The lattice fringe spacing of 0.232 and 0.175 nm is assigned to the (002) facet of Co(OH)₂ and the (012) facet of Ni(OH)₂, respectively (PDF#74-1057 and PDF#73-1520). Meanwhile, the (101) facet of Ru (0.205 nm) was also observed in high-resolution mode.

nodes.characterization_summary: Peaks at 3530 and 1625 cm⁻¹ for O-H bonds; peaks at 580-660 and 1058 cm⁻¹ for M-O and M-O-H bonds (M = Co or Ni).
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), the peaks observed at 3530 and 1625 cm⁻¹ for Ru@NF and Ni/Co(OH)₂-Ru@NF attribute to the O-H bonds assigned to adsorbed water molecules (Figure 2d). The peaks at 580-660 and 1058 cm⁻¹ of Ni/Co(OH)₂-Ru@NF are corresponded to the M-O bonds and the M-O-H bonds, respectively, proving the existence of metal hydroxides (M = Co or Ni).

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction characteristic peaks associated with Co(OH)₂, Ni(OH)₂ and Ru observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction characteristic peaks associated with Co(OH)₂, Ni(OH)₂ and Ru can be clearly attributed in Figure 2e.

nodes.characterization_summary: Peaks at 510 and 650 cm⁻¹ correspond to Co(OH)₂; Ni-OH at 318 cm⁻¹ and Ni-O at 456 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The co-existence of Co(OH)₂ and Ni(OH)₂ was additionally corroborated through Raman spectroscopy. Raman image displays that the peaks at 510 and 650 cm⁻¹ correspond to Co(OH)₂, and the peaks of the Ni-OH bond and the Ni-O bond are detected at 318 and 456 cm⁻¹, respectively (Figure 2f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p peaks at 463.1 and 485.4 eV (Ru⁰) and high-valent Ru⁸⁺; Co 2p peaks at 784.4/800.3 eV (Co²⁺) and 780.5/795.5 eV (Co³⁺); Ni 2p peaks at 860.3/879.6 eV (Ni²⁺) and 855.5/873.3 eV (Ni³⁺); O 1s peaks at 529.7 eV (M-OH) and 531.6 eV (oxygen vacancy).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface chemical states and valence state for the Ni/Co(OH)₂-Ru@NF were in-depth measured by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). ... From the high-resolution XPS spectrum of Ru 3p, the characteristic peaks of Ru⁰ are attributed at 463.1 and 485.4 eV. ... the Co 2p XPS spectrum can be observed in two sets of peaks corresponding to the Co²⁺ 2p₃/₂ (784.4 eV) and 2p₁/₂ (800.3 eV), and peaks at Co³⁺ 2p₃/₂ (780.5 eV) and 2p₁/₂ (795.5 eV). The Ni 2p XPS spectrum can be deconvolved as Ni²⁺ and Ni³⁺ peaks: 860.3 and 879.6 eV (Ni²⁺ 2p₃/₂ and 2p₁/₂) and 855.5 and 873.3 eV (Ni³⁺ 2p₃/₂ and 2p₁/₂). ... characteristic peaks of M-OH and oxygen vacancy are observed at 529.7 and 531.6 eV in the O 1s spectrum, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Prominent peaks at g = 2.003 indicating increased oxygen vacancies and higher electron density.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To demonstrate the existence of rich oxygen vacancy, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) was conducted ... The EPR spectrum of Ni/Co(OH)₂-Ru@NF exhibits prominent peaks at g = 2.003 compared to Ru@NF, suggesting an increased oxygen vacancies and higher electron density.
